Hi Laura — appreciate the clear questions. Below is a concise worked example and the logic we use so finance can map to your internal cost centers. Long version attached as an XLSX. Highlights: 1) Core nodes (reserved pool) — billed as a monthly platform fee that includes the reserved GPU footprint, platform licensing, and operator license per site. 2) Edge nodes (burst/burstable capacity or satellite sites) — billed as metered consumption (vGPU-hours) with a per-hour rate. 3) Volume breakpoints apply independently to the metered side and to the platform fee (we amortize the platform fee for committed cores). Example (3-site rollout):

- Baseline: 3 sites, each with 4 reserved GPUs = 12 reserved GPUs (core). Platform fee for reserved 12 GPUs: $38,400/month (calculated as $3,200 per reserved GPU equivalent per month amortized across operator license & infra).
- Edge / burst pool: assume average 600 vGPU-hours/month across all sites. Metered rate: $0.80 per vGPU-hour -> $480/month.

Discounting / breakpoints:
- Platform fee breakpoints (reserved GPUs): 0–24 GPUs (no volume discount), 25–99 GPUs (5% discount), >=100 GPUs (12% discount).
- Metered consumption breakpoints (vGPU-hours): 0–5k hrs (base rate), 5k–20k hrs (8% off base rate), >20k hrs (18% off base rate).

Support tiers interact like this: Standard support is included in the platform fee baseline. Premium support is a 12% uplift on the platform fee (covers 24x7 escalation + named SRE). The Premium uplift does not change metered unit pricing but does include a quarterly architecture review and an engineering runbook delivery.

Operational notes: platform fee is invoiced monthly and can be annualized on the PO (common for accounting). Metered usage is invoiced monthly in arrears. We can provide a blended invoice if your AP prefers a single line item.

Irene — copying you for any legal/SOW considerations. David — please confirm the amortization language below is acceptable for Helio. I can send a short SOW + pricing appendix for PO signature once Laura confirms the numbers look reasonable.

Best — Vivek
